children: By Anoop Menon

Dubai has 2.1 trillion UAE dirhams ($571.74 billion) worth of active projects underway, spanning real estate, aviation, transport, utilities, quality of life and other infrastructure sectors, according to an infographic shared on social media by the Dubai Media Office, citing figures disclosed at the Mohammed bin Rashid Leadership Forum.

The projects include AED 1.1 trillion in real estate developments through 2030, AED 128 billion for the expansion of Al Maktoum International Airport, AED 151 billion for new power and water grid infrastructure and AED 100 billion in projects undertaken by the Roads and Transport Authority (RTA).

Other major investments include AED 328 billion for the expansion of Emirates and flydubai's aircraft fleets, AED 18.7 billion for an Emirates engineering and maintenance complex, and more than AED 100 billion for the development of Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC).

The infrastructure pipeline also includes the AED 80 billion Dubai Strategic Sewerage Tunnels system, the AED 30 billion Tasreef stormwater drainage programme, the AED 10 billion expansion of Dubai Exhibition Centre and the AED 4 billion Dubai Blue and Green Spaces Roadmap.
The Mohammed bin Rashid Leadership Forum, held at Dubai World Trade Centre on Tuesday, brought together 1,000 senior government and private-sector leaders.

Commenting on Dubai's investment pipeline, Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister of the UAE and Ruler of Dubai, said the emirate's development momentum and ongoing achievements made it an ideal time to invest in Dubai and its infrastructure.
Transport and mobility

Mattar Al Tayer, Director General and Chairman of the Board of Executive Directors of RTA, said Dubai was developing an integrated mobility system covering transport in the air, at ground level and underground.

He said RTA was studying an integrated underground transport system to facilitate the movement of people, goods and services, create investment opportunities and improve the efficiency and sustainability of mobility.
Al Maktoum International Airport

Khalifa Al Zaffin, CEO of Dubai Aviation City Corporation and Dubai South, said Al Maktoum International Airport is being developed to accommodate 260 million passengers and 12 million tonnes of cargo annually.
The first phase aims to increase the airport's passenger handling capacity to approximately 150 million annually by 2032.
DIFC expansion

Essa Kazim, Governor of DIFC, said the DIFC Zabeel District development is scheduled for completion by 2040, with a gross development value exceeding AED 100 billion. Upon completion, the district is expected to accommodate more than 42,000 companies and a workforce exceeding 125,000 people, alongside more than 4,000 residential units.
Green infrastructure and smart construction

Marwan Ahmed bin Ghalita, Director General of Dubai Municipality, said Dubai plans to plant 3.5 million trees and expand green and landscaped areas to 187 square kilometres by 2040. The emirate is also targeting 95 million annual visits to its parks and recreational facilities.
He said the AED 30 billion Tasreef programme would increase the capacity of Dubai's stormwater drainage network by 700 percent upon completion.
Dubai is also targeting the use of modern and smart construction technologies in 40 percent of new buildings by 2033, he added.
(Writing by Anoop Menon; Editing by SA Kader)
